extracted.intended_audience: FFE State insurance regulators/plan management officials, HHS program staff, and QHP issuers
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and procedural requirements for Federally-facilitated Exchange (FFE) States to be designated as having an Effective ECP (Essential Community Provider) Review Program and thereby conduct ECP certification reviews of QHP issuers' plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Network plan reporting on contract offers (§156.235(a)(3) and (b)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: A network plan does not need to report on the status of contract negotiations for all available ECPs in their service area, but must at least report on the status of contract offers for all ECPs which the issuer has either included in its network plan or offered a contract to be included in its network plan within each service area.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies reporting burden: issuers need not track negotiations with every available ECP, only those they have included or offered a contract to (or offered to include) in each service area. Used to calculate satisfaction toward ECP thresholds and category/Indian health requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: FFE State eligibility to elect to conduct ECP certification reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Beginning PY 2027, FFE States, including States performing plan management, may elect to conduct their own ECP certification reviews provided the State demonstrates it has sufficient authority and the technical capacity to conduct these reviews by satisfying applicable criteria established by HHS to have an Effective ECP Review Program (proposed §155.1051).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a State does not submit interest/attestation, HHS will assume it prefers HHS to continue conducting reviews. HHS will notify States of determinations prior to the QHP certification cycle.

rubrics_metrics.name: State ECP requirements must be established in statute or regulation (§155.1051(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: FFE States with an Effective ECP Review Program must have established ECP requirements that are set forth in State statute or regulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These State requirements must ensure issuers meet requirements that promote a sufficient number and geographic distribution of ECPs, consistent with federal protections for low-income and medically underserved populations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency with federal ECP thresholds (§155.1051(c) — minimums to demonstrate)
rubrics_metrics.description: FFE States must demonstrate that their established ECP requirements ensure issuers meet: the minimum percentage requirements under §156.235(a)(2)(i), the Indian health care provider requirement under §156.235(a)(2)(ii)(A), and the category per county requirements for each of the eight ECP category types described under §156.235(a)(2)(ii)(B).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States may implement identical or alternative quantitative/qualitative approaches, but must show how those approaches maintain access comparable to the federal standards (e.g., 35% threshold example).

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance of alternative State ECP requirements (§155.1051(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: FFE States may have alternative, distinct ECP requirements tailored to local conditions, but must demonstrate how these requirements would promote a sufficient number and geographic distribution of ECPs to ensure reasonable and timely access to ECPs and adequate service for low-income enrollees or those in Health Professional Shortage Areas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States must submit a written description of the alternative requirements, explain how the State collects ECP data from issuers to measure compliance, and provide a detailed explanation of how the State uses this data to analyze access to ECPs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attestation and timing to HHS (apply prior to QHP certification cycle)
rubrics_metrics.description: An FFE State must express interest to HHS and submit an attestation for having an Effective ECP Review Program prior to the start of the QHP certification cycle for the first plan year it wishes to assume responsibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A State may attest for an Effective ECP Review Program, an Effective Provider Access Review Program, or both. HHS will review submissions to ensure the State has authority and capacity to conduct timely, effective reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-network plans: parity requirement for certification reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: If an FFE State elects to conduct ECP certification reviews and certifies non-network plans, the State must demonstrate it meets applicable criteria for both network plans and non-network plans (§155.1051(b)–(c)); a State cannot elect to conduct reviews only for network plans while certifying non-network plans (or vice versa).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a State does not intend to certify non-network plans at all, HHS will evaluate the State only on network plan criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: HHS notification, annual confirmation, and ongoing oversight (§155.1051(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: HHS will notify in writing whether an FFE State is determined to have an Effective ECP Review Program prior to the QHP certification cycle. Annually, HHS will confirm if the State wishes to continue conducting reviews and reserve the right to evaluate at any time whether the State continues to satisfy criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHS may perform environmental scans of State authorities, reevaluate designations if circumstances change, and provide technical assistance and resources to States.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factor 1: State legal authority to review ECP compliance (§155.1051(e)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: The State's legal authority to review whether plans applying for QHP certification meet ECP requirements, including relevant State regulations and statutes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Crucial to ensure the State has statutory/regulatory authority to promulgate ECP requirements and to enforce them through certification and follow-up actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factor 2: Evidence that State requirements are consistent with federal ECP aims (§155.1051(e)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Evidence that the State's requirements are consistent with ECP requirements under §155.1051(c)(1)–(c)(3) that promote a sufficient number and geographic distribution of ECPs, or the State's explanation/rationale for how its alternative requirements achieve the same goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to ensure State approaches maintain access comparable to §§156.235/156.236 and protect access for vulnerable populations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factor 3: State definition of an ECP if different from federal definition (§155.1051(e)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: A description of the State's definition of an ECP, if different from §156.235(c), including relevant categories and eligibility criteria the State uses to determine whether a facility qualifies as an ECP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledges States may expand or alter ECP categories; HHS needs to understand these differences to ensure statutory compliance (e.g., categories tied to 340B and Social Security Act citations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Factor 4: Process to identify qualified ECPs for network plans (§155.1051(e)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the State utilizes the Federal ECP List or has a process it uses to identify qualified ECPs that may be included within a network plan's provider network.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critical for the State to identify exact geographic location and distribution of ECPs to highlight those available in an issuer's service area for contracting and to ensure representation across ECP categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factor 5: Process to identify qualified ECPs for non-network plans (§155.1051(e)(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the State utilizes the Federal ECP List or has a process it uses to identify qualified ECPs that may accept a non-network plan's benefit amount as payment in full.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Important for certifying non-network plans because access depends on ECPs that will accept benefit amounts in full; identification supports accurate assessment of access under non-network models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factor 6: Data collection systems and methodologies (§155.1051(e)(6))
rubrics_metrics.description: A description of data collection systems, resources, templates, or methodologies used by the State to collect and review ECP data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrates technical capacity to efficiently collect large, complex issuer ECP data and meaningfully apply assessment methodologies to measure access across the State (e.g., use of ECP List, templates, MPMS tools).

rubrics_metrics.name: Factor 7: Collection of contract offer status and benefit-amount offers (§155.1051(e)(7))
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the State generally collects information from QHP issuers regarding the status of contract offers for network plans or offers of benefit amounts as payment in full to an ECP for non-network plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This data allows the State to validate issuer progress toward contracting with ECPs and measure compliance with thresholds and category/Indian health requirements based on offers/executed contracts and benefit-amount offers accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factor 8: Delegation of review authority (§155.1051(e)(8))
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the State has delegated authority to some other entity other than the State Department of Insurance to perform any or all ECP review activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States must report delegated arrangements so HHS understands who handles ECP review data and whether delegated entities have sufficient expertise and capacity to conduct reviews consistent with program criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factor 9: Compliance reviews, enforcement, and remediation processes (§155.1051(e)(9))
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the State has compliance reviews, follow-up procedures, and enforcement frameworks applicable to issuers that demonstrate inadequate networks of ECPs or inadequate access to ECPs that accept benefit amounts as payment in full, including standardized processes to assess issuer efforts to come into compliance and any justification/exception processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evidence of enforcement authority and standardized remediation processes is critical to ensure issuers can be brought into compliance and that certification reviews have integrity and enforceable outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factor 10: Consumer complaint monitoring and response process (§155.1051(e)(10))
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the State has a process for monitoring and addressing consumer-related complaints regarding access to ECPs to ensure sufficient access consistent with section 1311(c)(1)(C) of the Affordable Care Act and State statute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrates ongoing monitoring capability (e.g., handling facility closures, provider terminations, inaccurate directories, appointment availability) and a mechanism to detect and remediate access issues during plan years.

rubrics_metrics.name: HHS-provided resources and technical assistance
rubrics_metrics.description: HHS will be available to provide technical assistance and will continue to make ECP resources publicly available (Final Plan Year ECP List, Rolling Draft ECP List, QHP/SADP ECP tools, Available ECP Write-in List, Plan Validation workspace in MPMS, guidance on QHP website) for States, including those designated as Effective ECP Review Program States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States may leverage these resources for identification of ECPs, data collection, and assessment methodologies; HHS expects many States and issuers already use these tools.
